task: Check Boeing for material events since 2026-09-21

merged.claim: On 2026-10-20, the FAA certified the Boeing 737-10 (737 MAX 10) with an amended type certificate, clearing Boeing to begin deliveries in the coming months.
On 2026-10-05, Boeing received a seven-year contract from Lockheed Martin, worth about $14.7 billion (undefinitized), to accelerate and triple PAC-3 MSE seeker production.
On 2026-09-30, Ethiopian Airlines ordered eight 777-8 Freighters and two 777 Freighters from Boeing, the first African carrier to order the 777-8F.

On 2026-09-29, the U.S. Navy selected Boeing for the F/A-XX sixth-generation carrier fighter program, a multi-billion-dollar contract (full-scale development reported at over $20 billion) to design, build and deliver the aircraft replacing the F/A-18 Super Hornet.

On 2026-09-28, the FAA delayed certification of Boeing's 737 MAX 10 pending resolution of a software issue affecting automated flight guidance in a go-around/landing scenario; Boeing shares closed down 6.9%.
On 2026-09-29, the FAA opened a review of a Boeing 737 MAX software issue that could disengage automated vertical navigation during a go-around and said 737 MAX 10 certification would be delayed.
On 2026-09-23, Boeing and Turkish Airlines finalized an order for up to 150 737 MAX jets (100 737-8 plus options for 50).
On 2026-09-23, Biman Bangladesh Airlines ordered 11 more Boeing jets (five 787-10s and six 737-8s), bringing its Boeing order book to 25 aircraft.

On 2026-09-21, the FAA proposed an airworthiness directive requiring inspections and possible corrective actions for elevator-buss assembly bearings on certain Boeing 737-8, 737-9 and 737-8200 aircraft.
On 2026-10-09, a King County judge rejected Boeing's effort to block punitive damages in the 47-plaintiff lawsuit over the 2024 Alaska Airlines 737 MAX door-plug incident.
On 2026-10-17, Boeing was reported to be weighing closure of its Ridley Park, Pennsylvania helicopter facility due to uncertain Army funding, putting roughly 3,000 jobs at risk.
On 2026-10-08, the FAA published a final airworthiness directive requiring hardware and maintenance changes on Boeing 787 aircraft to address an undetected slat-position hazard; effective 2026-11-12.
On 2026-10-02, the FAA's safety review found the Boeing 737 MAX 10 software glitch is not a flight-safety issue, removing the software-related obstacle to certification.
On 2026-09-29, Boeing won a $2.38 billion additional F-15EX contract covering 22 more aircraft for the U.S. Air Force.

nimble.claim: On 2026-10-20, the U.S. FAA certified Boeing's 737-10, the largest member of the 737 MAX family, clearing it for delivery weeks after a software-related certification delay.
On 2026-10-05, Boeing received a seven-year contract to accelerate production of PAC-3 Missile Segment Enhancement (MSE) seekers.
On 2026-09-30, Ethiopian Airlines ordered Boeing 777 and 777-8 freighters to expand its cargo fleet.

On 2026-09-29, the U.S. Navy selected Boeing for the F/A-XX sixth-generation carrier fighter program, a multi-billion-dollar contract to design, build and deliver the aircraft to replace the F/A-18 Super Hornet; it is Boeing's second sixth-generation fighter selection after the Air Force's F-47 award in 2025.

On 2026-09-28, the FAA said it would delay certifying Boeing's 737 MAX 10 until a newly disclosed software issue (potentially blocking pilots' access to automated flight guidance in a specific landing scenario) is resolved; Boeing shares closed down 6.9%.
On 2026-09-23, Boeing and Turkish Airlines finalized an order for up to 150 737 MAX jets.
On 2026-09-23, Biman Bangladesh Airlines ordered five Boeing 787-10 and six 737-8 jets, bringing its Boeing order book to 25 jets following an earlier 14-jet order this year.

exa.claim: On 2026-09-21, the FAA proposed an airworthiness directive requiring inspections and possible corrective actions for elevator-buss assembly bearings on certain Boeing 737-8, 737-9 and 737-8200 aircraft, creating potential compliance and fleet-maintenance costs.

On 2026-09-29, the FAA opened a review of a Boeing 737 MAX software issue that could disengage automated vertical navigation during a go-around and said Boeing 737 MAX 10 certification would be delayed, threatening certification timing and potentially deliveries.

On 2026-09-29, the U.S. Navy awarded Boeing the F/A-XX sixth-generation fighter program, with the full-scale development phase valued at more than $20 billion, establishing a major long-term defense franchise.

On 2026-09-30, Ethiopian Airlines ordered eight Boeing 777-8 Freighters and two 777 Freighters, expanding Boeing's 777X and freighter backlog and making Ethiopian the first African carrier to purchase the 777-8 Freighter.

On 2026-10-05, Lockheed Martin awarded Boeing a seven-year contract worth about $14.7 billion to scale and deliver Patriot PAC-3 MSE seekers, supporting a production tripling and substantial defense revenue visibility.

On 2026-10-09, a King County judge rejected Boeing's effort to block punitive damages in the 47-plaintiff lawsuit over the 2024 Alaska Airlines 737 MAX door-plug incident, increasing Boeing's litigation exposure.

On 2026-10-17, Boeing was reported to be weighing closure of its Ridley Park, Pennsylvania helicopter facility because of uncertain Army funding, putting roughly 3,000 jobs and the site's future at risk.

parallel.claim: On 2026-10-20, the FAA certified the Boeing 737 MAX 10, issuing an amended type certificate and production authorization and clearing a major regulatory hurdle for Boeing's largest MAX variant.

On 2026-10-08, the FAA published a final airworthiness directive requiring hardware and maintenance changes on Boeing 787 aircraft to address an undetected slat-position hazard that could prevent continued safe flight; effective 2026-11-12.
On 2026-10-05, Boeing announced that Lockheed Martin awarded it an approximately $14.7 billion undefinitized contract action under a seven-year framework to triple PAC-3 MSE seeker production.
On 2026-10-02, the FAA's safety review found that the Boeing 737 MAX 10 software glitch is not a flight-safety issue, removing the software-related obstacle to MAX 10 certification.
On 2026-09-30, Ethiopian Airlines placed a firm order with Boeing for eight 777-8 Freighters and two 777 Freighters, making it the first African customer for the 777-8 Freighter.
On 2026-09-29, the U.S. Navy selected Boeing for the F/A-XX program, a multibillion-dollar contract to design, build and deliver the Navy's next-generation fighter.
On 2026-09-29, Boeing won a $2.38 billion additional F-15EX contract covering 22 more aircraft for the U.S. Air Force.
On 2026-09-28, the FAA delayed Boeing 737 MAX 10 certification pending review of a navigation-software fault that could interrupt automated guidance during a go-around.

firecrawl.claim: On 2026-09-23, Boeing and Turkish Airlines finalized an order for up to 150 737 MAX jets (100 737-8 plus options for 50 more), the airline's largest Boeing single-aisle order.
On 2026-09-23, Biman Bangladesh Airlines ordered 11 more Boeing jets (five 787-10s and six 737-8s), bringing its Boeing order book to 25 aircraft.

On 2026-09-28, the FAA paused certification of Boeing's 737 MAX 10 while a software issue affecting automated flight guidance in a specific go-around scenario was resolved, creating timing and delivery risk.

On 2026-09-29, the U.S. Navy selected Boeing for the F/A-XX sixth-generation fighter program, a multi-billion-dollar contract to design, build and deliver the aircraft meant to replace F/A-18 Super Hornets.
On 2026-09-30, Ethiopian Airlines placed a firm order with Boeing for eight 777-8 Freighters and two 777 Freighters, making it the first African carrier to order the 777-8F.

On 2026-10-05, Boeing received an approximately $14.7 billion undefinitized contract from Lockheed Martin under a seven-year framework to triple PAC-3 MSE seeker production, with hundreds of related jobs expected in Huntsville.
On 2026-10-20, the FAA certified the Boeing 737-10 (amended type certificate), clearing Boeing to begin deliveries in the coming months; more than 30 customers have ordered 1,555 of the model.

c1.note: Boeing's press release, dated 2026-10-20, says the FAA certified the 737-10 and that deliveries can begin in the coming months.

c2.note: Boeing's press release, dated 2026-10-05, confirms the roughly $14.7B undefinitized Lockheed contract to triple PAC-3 MSE seeker output. The page says the contract sits inside a seven-year framework agreement.

c3.note: Boeing's press release, dated 2026-09-30, confirms Ethiopian ordered eight 777-8F and two 777F, and is the first African buyer of the 777-8F. Ten freighters is a modest order, but it is a customer win.

c4.note: Boeing's press release, dated 2026-09-29, confirms the Navy selected it for F/A-XX. The page says only "billions"; I did not verify the reported figure of more than $20B.

c5.note: The Reuters report on CTV, dated 2026-09-28, confirms the FAA delay and a share drop of about 7%. The page did not give the software cause, and the CNBC page returned 403.

c6.note: CBS (updated 9/29) confirms the FAA review of the VNAV go-around software issue and a delay to MAX 10 certification. The FAA statements were likely made 9/28, which is still after the since-date.

c7.note: Boeing's release dated 9/23 confirms 100 737-8s plus 50 options. It is a large customer win.

c8.note: The order is real and dated 9/23, but 11 jets from a small carrier is a minor order and not a major customer win.

c9.note: The NPRM is real, but it is dated 9/21, the since-date itself rather than after it. It is also a routine proposed AD covering 95 US-registered aircraft, so it is not material.

c10.note: A search summary of the Axios article (the page itself was blocked) says Judge Hecklinger ruled on the Friday before 10/14, which is 10/9. She declined to block punitive damages in the 47-plaintiff suit, which adds litigation exposure.

c11.note: The article says Boeing is only weighing a possible closure, with no decision and no announcement. It expects to review next year's budget and decide within a few years. The roughly 3,000 jobs figure is correct. The claim describes a real report, but it is soft for a plant-closure event.

c12.note: AD 2026-20-10 is real and effective 2026-11-12. It is a routine airworthiness directive and does not fit the material-event definition as regulatory action against the company.

c13.note: Search results show the FAA said on 2026-10-02 that the software glitch is not a safety concern. That clears an obstacle to MAX 10 certification. The CNBC page returned 403, so I relied on Reuters-based coverage.

c14.note: Boeing's page confirms a $2.38B contract for 22 more F-15EX for the USAF, dated 2026-09-29.

c2.note: Boeing's press release dated 2026-10-05 confirms an undefinitized contract from Lockheed Martin worth about $14.7B to triple PAC-3 MSE seeker output, under a seven-year framework. The release doesn't say whether seven years is the contract's own term. The deal is material and falls after the since-date.

c7.note: Boeing's press release dated 2026-09-23 confirms Turkish Airlines finalized an order for 100 737-8 jets plus options for 50, up to 150 in total. It is the airline's largest Boeing single-aisle order, making it material, and the date is after the since-date.
